Heading: Research on Sustainable Construction Materials
Introduction: Our research examines local clays, supplementary cementitious materials and low-carbon cement and concrete. We study chemical and mineralogical properties of clays and SCMs include fly ash, slag, glass powder, and etc., hydration, strength, durability and also study thermo-mechanochemical activation to understand how material composition and processing affect performance.

tables.current: Detailed information regarding LC3 technology guidance, development, and implementation support.
tables.approved: Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3) combines clinker, calcined clay, limestone and gypsum to reduce clinker use. We assess local clay suitability, optimise calcination and binder composition, and evaluate mortar and concrete performance. Our team’s experience includes national clay exploration, LC3 research and demonstration at NED UET, and technical work with Cherat Cement and Power Cement. We support laboratory development, staff training and the preparation and evaluation of pilot or plant trials, according to the agreed project scope.

tables.current: Details will be added by the NC4SCM team / Client input.
tables.approved:
• Clay surveys, sampling and raw-material screening.
• Chemical, mineralogical and thermal characterisation using XRF, XRD and DTG–TGA.
• Calcination trials, grinding and particle-size assessment.
• Reactivity assessment using R3, and methylene blue value testing, interpreted alongside mineralogy and performance data.
• Binder formulation, gypsum adjustment and mortar/concrete mix design optimization.
• Hydration, strength and durability evaluation.
• Technical assessment and monitoring of pilot or plant trials.

tables.current: Evidence-led assessment of clays and supplementary cementitious materials.
tables.approved: We characterise clays, limestone, fly ash, cement and other candidate construction materials to assess their suitability for cementitious applications. Chemical composition, mineral phases, thermal behaviour and particle size are considered together with reactivity, hydration and performance results. This helps identify suitable materials, compare sources and select processing conditions. The test programme is tailored to the material and the client’s technical question, with specialist analyses coordinated through collaborating laboratories when required.

tables.current: Details will be added by the NC4SCM team / Client input.
tables.approved:
• X-ray fluorescence (XRF) for chemical composition.
• X-ray diffraction (XRD) for mineral phase identification.
• DTG–TGA and loss on ignition for thermal changes and mass loss.
• FTIR and SEM–EDS for complementary structural and microstructural assessment.
• Particle-size distribution and fineness assessment.
• Isothermal calorimetry for hydration behaviour and R3 reactivity.
• Methylene blue value testing for supplementary screening.
• Interpretation of results alongside mortar/concrete performance.

tables.current: Applied research for lower-carbon, affordable construction materials.
tables.approved: We develop and evaluate cementitious materials through laboratory trials and performance testing. Our work includes LC3, activation of heterogeneous clays, fly ash, and other supplementary cementitious materials, recycled aggregate concrete and self-healing concrete. We examine how composition, processing and mix proportions affect hydration, strength and durability. Development begins with material assessment and proceeds through formulation and testing. Promising formulations can then be considered for demonstration or industrial validation, based on the results and project requirements.

tables.current: Details will be added by the NC4SCM team / Client input.
tables.approved:
• Screening of local and alternative raw materials.
• Thermal and mechanochemical clay activation studies.
• Binder formulation and mortar/concrete mix design.
• Experimental comparisons and optimisation of material proportions.
• Hydration, compressive, tensile and flexural testing.
• Selected durability tests, including absorption, chloride-related testing and carbonation.
• Research on elevated-temperature performance and self-healing behaviour.
• Demonstration and trial planning for promising formulations.

tables.current: Research-to-industry support for validation, scale-up, and adoption.
tables.approved: We help industry partners translate laboratory findings into practical decisions on raw materials, processing and product development. Support includes LC3 feasibility assessment, technical review of clay calcination and grinding options, trial preparation, performance monitoring and staff training. Our experience includes cement-plant consultancy and coordination between researchers, plant teams and technology providers. Recommendations reflect the available evidence, plant conditions and agreed scope, with further trials proposed where additional validation is needed.
